keys.description: shared internal secret the /internal/validate endpoint requires (fail-closed guard, main.py). Unset, gateway's validation hop 503s and every API-key check fails — so the boot refuses instead of coming up green and rejecting every call (the 2026-04-23 failure shape, #526). The same value gates /internal/bootstrap-admin and /internal/users/by-email, so a published placeholder is refused outright (F95).

keys.default: (unset — every client route answers 401; /admin/*, /internal/*, /health and /metrics are unaffected)
keys.description: §1.10, §6.9 F-E: the key ring the gateway signs x-user-id with, the same ring the gateway holds, in the webhook secret encryption ring's format: JSON {"<kid>": "<exactly 32 bytes, base64>"}, a kid being 1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -. app/identity_guard.py checks x-gateway-signature: kid=<kid>,t=<unix>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256> under the key its kid names, over the kid, t, x-user-id and every other identity header the gateway forwards (email, scopes, limits, workspaces, webhook url, secret and events), method, body SHA-256, raw query and path (core/gateway/contracts/gateway-identity), and refuses with 401 a signature that is missing, malformed, under a kid not in this ring, wrong for any of those, or more than GATEWAY_IDENTITY_MAX_SKEW_S seconds from this clock. Unset or malformed, every client request is refused and the rejection log names the fault, never a key.

§1.10, §6.9 F-E: app/identity_guard.py refuses with 401 a gateway signature whose t is more than this many seconds before or after this service's clock (the replay window); the same setting on meeting-api and admin-api. Not a positive whole number, the guard is not built (a ValueError naming the setting) and no client request is served.

keys.default: (unset — the admin surface then answers 500 'Admin authentication is not configured')
keys.description: admin bearer for the privileged admin surface (main.py:_admin_token → os.getenv, NO code default; every /admin route and the key-minting surface behind it). It read 'changeme' here, which described the deploy surfaces rather than the code — and that is exactly what a published default is: this token MINTS AN API KEY FOR ANY USER, so a stack left on the literal hands the whole account plane to anyone who read the repository. Same refusal INTERNAL_API_SECRET got in F95, for a strictly larger blast radius (A19).

SQLAlchemy async-engine pool_size (persistent connections per pod). Pure runtime override — reconcile with deploy/db-budget.json (Σ replicas × (pool_size + max_overflow) + reserved ≤ max_connections) on managed Postgres. #635.
SQLAlchemy async-engine max_overflow (burst connections above pool_size per pod). Pure runtime override — reconcile with deploy/db-budget.json. #635.

bounded initial-DB-connect retry: max attempts before failing loud. On a cold start where Postgres DNS isn't resolvable yet, the boot retries the first connect instead of exit(3)-ing into the k8s restart loop (#901). After this many attempts it re-raises.
bounded initial-DB-connect retry: base backoff seconds (capped-exponential: base×2^(n-1), clamped to DB_CONNECT_MAX_DELAY). #901.
bounded initial-DB-connect retry: max backoff seconds per attempt (the exponential is clamped here). #901.

flows' intake, told that a person finished onboarding. IDENTITY TELLS FLOWS; IT DOES NOT ASK IT — the publish is best-effort, bounded at 2s and swallowed, so a deployment with no flows domain onboards people exactly as one with a flows domain does, and so does one where flows is simply down. Unset is therefore not a degraded state, it is a profile. The fact itself is stamped on the person in the same transaction as the account, so the record survives a publish that never lands (app/events.py, app/main.py POST /admin/users). Spelled bare FLOWS_API_URL until F208 — the only one of the three flows publishers not carrying the VEXA_ prefix this repo uses for its own keys; app/events.py still reads that name for one release, with a boot warning, so an unmigrated deployment keeps publishing.

operator key for the same edge, sent as X-Flows-Operator-Key (flows' POST /events is authenticated). The header was spelled X-Flows-Admin-Key until #1486 and flows still accepts that name for one release; admin-api sends only the new one. Declared as part of the edge rather than beside it: a publish target without its credential is a publish that always 401s, and the pair is what makes the edge real. Unset alongside an unset URL is the no-flows profile; unset with a URL set is a deployment whose facts are being refused, which is why both are visible on one declaration.

meeting-api base URL for the one call admin-api makes to it: POST /internal/webhooks/test (with INTERNAL_API_SECRET), which queues the webhook.test send behind POST /v2/webhooks/{id}/test (§2.7). Unreachable, that route answers 503 unavailable; nothing else depends on it.

webhooks (§1.13): per-account quota of webhook subscriptions; POST /v2/webhooks past it is refused with 429 quota_exceeded (no Retry-After). Not a whole number of at least 1, admin-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.13): the daily retention sweep (app/retention.py, single-flight) deletes deliveries in a final state (delivered, failed, dead, cancelled) older than this many days, their attempts with them, then published outbox rows with no deliveries left; unpublished outbox rows are never pruned. Not a positive whole number, admin-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.13, §6.9 F-I): the daily retention sweep (app/retention.py) deletes old final deliveries, then published outbox rows with no deliveries left, at most this many rows per batch, each batch its own transaction. Not a positive whole number, admin-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.13, §6.9 F-I): the per-run cap of the daily retention sweep: at most this many batches of each delete a run; a run that reaches it logs a warning, counts aw_sweep_runs_total{sweep="webhook-retention",result="capped"} and leaves the rest to the next run. Not a positive whole number, admin-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§2.7): comma-separated hosts a subscription URL may name although they are private (compared case-insensitively, never resolved); every other private, loopback, link-local or internal target is refused on save. meeting-api applies the same list on every send.

keys.default: (unset — with WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_ACTIVE_KEY also unset, the webhook routes that store or read a secret answer 503 unavailable)
keys.description: webhooks (§2.7): the key ring subscription secrets are encrypted under, JSON {"<id>": "<32 bytes, base64>"} (AES-256-GCM; app/secret_box.py). Set with a malformed ring, a key that is not exactly 32 bytes, or without WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_ACTIVE_KEY, admin-api refuses to start. meeting-api holds the same ring to decrypt at signing time.

webhooks (§2.7): the id in WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_KEYS new secrets are encrypted under; rows under another id are re-encrypted under it on their next internal read. Must name a key in the ring, or admin-api refuses to start.
